text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attock Refinery Ltd and Pakistan Refinery Ltd have signed two separate agreements worth $110 million to upgrade refining capacities.
- Naval Chief Admiral Mansoorul Haq has resigned after being ordered by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif to step down in the backdrop of alleged corruption allegations.

- Pakistan has resented the U.S. Foreign Relations Committee Chairman's move to seek termination of peace-keeping role of the U.N. Military Observers Group along the Line of Control dividing disputed Jammu and Kashmir state between India and Pakistan.
- Lt-Gen Ali Quli Khan has been appointed Chief of General Staff in place of Lt-Gen Iftikhar who retires on May 15.
- Protesters blocked the Mingora-Bahrain Road in protest against wheat flour shortages.

- Pakistan has dismissed as "out of place" an Indian minister's proposal for a confederation among Bangladesh, India and Pakistan, saying New Delhi and Islamabad should instead tackle problems plaguing their ties.
- The arrest of Squadron Leader Farooq Ahmed in the United States for heroin smuggling could lead to pressure from Washington to renegotiate the extradition treaty between the two countries.
- The government has turned down a request from the Water and Power Development Authority for bridge financing of 1.5 billion rupees for the 1,450-megawatt Ghazi Barotha Hydro-power project.
- The government has decided to make privatisation procedures more transparent and profit-oriented.
- Pakistan Steel is trying to attract foreign investment for an expansion plan to absorb surplus staff.
- The government has set up two committees to devise plans to accelerate oil and gas exploration.
